sections.title: The letter i
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (i) /i/. Its main sound is a close front vowel, as in (ici) /i.si/, which means here. A vowel is a sound made with open air. This letter makes two sounds in French.

sections.title: Mouth shape
paragraphs: For the first sound, spread your lips wide and raise your tongue very high. Keep your tongue tense and near the front teeth. For the second sound, make the mouth narrower and let the tongue rise quickly toward the hard roof. Touch your throat to feel the voice run smoothly.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: This letter usually gives a pure vowel sound, as in (île) /il/. You also hear this sound with an accent mark. When it stands right before another vowel, it turns into a quick semivowel, as in (ciel) /sjɛl/. You also hear that gliding sound at the start of (hier) /jɛʁ/.

sections.title: Common pitfalls
paragraphs: Do not make this vowel weak and loose like the sound in English sit. Keep your tongue high and tense, like the vowel in see, but keep it short. Never turn the sound into a glide unless another vowel follows immediately. Keep your lips flat and wide.
